reason: If they earn enough, fine, pay some back. But a limit, so it doesn't crush anyone starting out.
They were waiting and not allowed to work. Charging them for that feels wrong to me.
Support while waiting is part of a fair system. I would not bill people who fled.
The taxpayer paid, so they should pay it back. A mortgage is not optional for me either.
Pay what you can afford. A cap is fair, and I would not ask more than that.
I've paid in all my life. Anyone who got help should pay the full amount back.
Make it depend on what they earn. Some can pay, some can't, and it should be capped.
Take it from wages once they have a job, not before. Then they can stand up first.
Repayment should be based on income with a ceiling, so it is fair to both sides.
People who flee should not start life in debt to the state. Drop it.
It was public money. Repay all of it, whatever they earn.
Pay through tax when working. It is simple and nobody is chased while out of work.
